Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pdecompR 0.1.0

  • First version. A pure R finite-element framework for two-dimensional scalar PDEs:
    • domains (rectangles, simple polygons), structured and polygon triangular meshes with validation, quality measures and named boundary markers, Gmsh 2.2 and 4.1 import, VTK export;
    • continuous Lagrange P1 and P2 elements, Gaussian quadrature on intervals and triangles, sparse assembly through ‘Matrix’;
    • Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin conditions, pure Neumann problems with compatibility checks and a zero-mean gauge;
    • linear elasticity with vector-valued P1 and P2 displacements, plane strain and plane stress, displacement (including roller) and traction conditions;
    • elliptic (diffusion, advection with optional SUPG, reaction), heat and general parabolic (backward Euler, Crank-Nicolson), reaction-diffusion systems (IMEX and Newton), quasilinear and p-Laplace solvers;
    • a weak-form language (trial_function(), grad(), dot(), integrate_domain(), integrate_boundary());
    • error norms, convergence studies, a residual error estimator, Doerfler marking and newest vertex bisection;
    • discrete forward and adjoint sensitivities, parameter estimation and distributed optimal control.
  • Robustness before release:
    • singular systems are detected from the assembled operator: Robin conditions with alpha = 0, variational problems, advection with zero-flux boundaries (left null vector compatibility) and elasticity constraints that leave a rigid motion;
    • linear solves that do not reach their tolerance give a warning, and iterative solvers guard against breakdown and zero right-hand sides;
    • the error estimator evaluates the diffusion on each side of an edge, gives Dirichlet conditions precedence as the solver does, and measures how well the space represents Dirichlet data;
    • finite-element coefficients and initial data are evaluated on their own space, so they may come from another mesh or degree; errornorm() accepts a reference fe_function;
    • time-dependent Neumann and Robin data work in heat and reaction-diffusion problems; only a third argument named t makes a function time dependent;
    • Crank-Nicolson starts with two backward Euler steps (startup) to damp oscillations from rough initial data;
    • the weak-form language rejects products of directional derivatives, gradients of coefficient products and mixed function spaces;
    • SUPG accepts tensor diffusion; P2 functions are plotted on subdivided elements; plots compose with par(mfrow = ...); write_vtk() writes displacement vectors and time-dependent solutions;
    • stricter input checks for reaction-diffusion species, boundary edges, observations, Dirichlet values, polygon size and Gmsh files.

Additional features

  • manufactured_solution() derives source terms and gradients symbolically with ‘symcompR’ (optional) for verification studies.
  • Mesh regions: pde_mesh(regions = ), set_region(), mesh_regions(), Gmsh physical surfaces, and region_coefficient() for piecewise coefficients that keep their geometry under refinement.
  • elasticity_stress() returns strains, stresses and the von Mises stress per element or averaged to vertices; write_vtk(stress = TRUE) writes them.
  • write_vtk() writes P2 data on quadratic triangles (VTK cell type 22).
  • Parabolic problems accept time-dependent diffusion, advection and reaction coefficients (reassembled each step, second order with Crank-Nicolson).
  • Heat and reaction-diffusion solutions record the integral of each species at the stored times (diagnostics$integral), shown by summary().
  • Direct solvers report "singular" when the factorization has a pivot ratio near machine precision; nonlinear problems without Dirichlet, Robin or reaction terms stop with a message.
  • benchmarks/reference-problems.R runs the ten reference problems and records errors, observed orders, timings and peak memory.
